package_info.package_versions: 7.69.0 up to and including 8.3.0 (CVE-2023-38545); 7.9.1 up to and including 8.3.0 (CVE-2023-38546)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of curl/libcurl contain a critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability (CVE-2023-38545) in the SOCKS5 proxy handshake logic. When connecting to an attacker-controlled HTTP server via a SOCKS5 proxy with remote hostname resolution (socks5h://), improper bounds checking allows an attacker to supply an overlong hostname, resulting in a heap overflow. This can be exploited to cause denial of service or potentially achieve remote code execution.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when making a network request via SOCKS5 proxy with remote hostname resolution enabled, e.g., socks5h://)
execution_context.file_location: libcurl source code, SOCKS5 state machine logic (typically in url.c or socks.c)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a network request is made via a SOCKS5 proxy with remote hostname resolution and the supplied hostname exceeds 255 bytes, the code attempts to fall back to local resolution, but later constructs a SOCKS5 protocol frame by copying the overlong hostname into a fixed-size heap buffer, resulting in a heap buffer overflow.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code fails to enforce the SOCKS5 protocol's 255-byte hostname limit, allowing an overlong hostname to be processed and copied into a buffer without proper bounds checking, which can be exploited for heap overflow attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal protocol handling would strictly reject or truncate hostnames longer than 255 bytes, preventing any buffer overflows or unsafe memory operations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code would validate input lengths and reject overlong hostnames, never allowing unchecked memory copies that could overflow buffers.
key_indicators: Improper bounds checking on hostname length in SOCKS5 handshake
Heap buffer overflow due to unchecked memcpy or similar operation
Protocol fallback logic that does not prevent unsafe memory operations when handling overlong hostnames

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when following an HTTP 30x redirect from an attacker-controlled server)
execution_context.file_location: libcurl HTTP redirect handling logic (e.g., http.c or transfer.c)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Location: https://aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa/ (host name can be extended up to 64KB)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the client receives an HTTP 30x redirect with a Location header containing an excessively long hostname, the client processes the redirect and attempts to connect to the new hostname via a SOCKS5 proxy with remote hostname resolution, causing the vulnerable state machine to process the overlong hostname and trigger a heap buffer overflow.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of an extremely long hostname in the Location header is crafted to exploit memory handling bugs in the client, specifically targeting the SOCKS5 proxy logic to trigger a heap overflow.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal HTTP redirects use valid, reasonably sized hostnames; overlong hostnames should be rejected or sanitized before further processing.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for HTTP redirects with hostnames exceeding protocol limits; such behavior is only seen in exploit attempts.
key_indicators: HTTP 30x redirect with Location header containing a hostname longer than 255 bytes
Interaction with SOCKS5 proxy using remote hostname resolution (socks5h://) immediately after processing the redirect

attack_chain.action: Attacker sets up a malicious HTTP server that issues an HTTP 30x redirect with a Location header containing an overlong hostname (exceeding 255 bytes).
attack_chain.leads_to: Client processes the redirect and prepares to connect to the attacker-supplied overlong hostname via a SOCKS5 proxy.

attack_chain.action: Client (curl/libcurl) processes the redirect and attempts to connect to the attacker-supplied hostname using a SOCKS5 proxy with remote hostname resolution (socks5h://).
attack_chain.leads_to: Heap buffer overflow is triggered in the client, potentially leading to denial of service or remote code execution.

behavioral_signatures: SOCKS5 proxy usage with remote hostname resolution (socks5h:// scheme or CURLPROXY_SOCKS5_HOSTNAME option)
HTTP 30x redirects with Location headers containing hostnames longer than 255 bytes
Heap buffer overflows or segmentation faults in curl/libcurl processes following SOCKS5 proxy connections
network_indicators: Outbound connections to SOCKS5 proxies using the socks5h:// scheme
HTTP 30x redirects with Location headers containing hostnames longer than 255 bytes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for use of the socks5h:// scheme in curl/libcurl invocations, either via command-line flags (--socks5-hostname, -x socks5h://) or API usage (CURLPROXY_SOCKS5_HOSTNAME). Inspect HTTP traffic for 30x redirects with abnormally long hostnames in the Location header. Watch for segmentation faults or abnormal crashes in curl/libcurl processes, especially when interacting with SOCKS5 proxies. Use static analysis to flag code that sets CURLOPT_PROXYTYPE to CURLPROXY_SOCKS5_HOSTNAME or uses socks5h:// in proxy settings. Correlate crash reports with recent SOCKS5 proxy activity and overlong hostnames in network logs.
